cards.text: Our story picks up with Samuel, the man who's been leading Israel. And Samuel has grown OLD. I bet his knees crack louder than my oven door, so it's time to hand the job down.

cards.question: Samuel is old and ready to pass the job on. Who does he appoint as judges over Israel?

cards.text: His firstborn is Joel, and his second is Abijah. They set up as judges in Beersheba. Now let's see how the boys do.

cards.question: Samuel's sons Joel and Abijah walk in their father's ways.
Samuel's sons turn aside toward dishonest gain. What do they do as judges?

answers.text: They accept bribes and pervert justice
They stop holding court at all
They hand the land to the Philistines

cards.text: Judges taking bribes. That's a referee showing up in one team's jersey. So all the elders of Israel gather together and come to Samuel at Ramah.

cards.question: The elders tell Samuel he's old and his sons don't walk in his ways. So what do they ask Samuel to appoint?
The elders want a king to judge them, just like all the other ___.

cards.text: 'Give us a king to judge us.' Ooh. Samuel did NOT like that. The text says their demand was displeasing in his sight.

cards.question: When the elders' demand displeases him, Samuel storms out on them.

cards.text: Nope. Samuel takes it to the LORD in prayer. And the LORD tells him to listen to the voice of the people in all that they say.

cards.question: The LORD tells Samuel it isn't Samuel the people have rejected. They've rejected the LORD as their ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD looks way back. All the way to the day He brought them up out of Egypt.

cards.question: The LORD says the people have been forsaking Him and serving other gods ever since He brought them out of Egypt.

cards.text: And now they're doing the same to Samuel. So here's the LORD's answer: listen to their voice. But there's more to it, friend.

cards.question: The LORD tells Samuel to listen to the people. What else must Samuel do?

answers.text: Solemnly warn them what the king will be like
Make them fast and pray for forty days
Choose the king from his own family

cards.text: Samuel goes to the people asking him for a king and speaks all the words of the LORD. Here's what life under a king will look like.

cards.question: Samuel starts describing the king. What will the king do with the people's sons?

answers.text: Put them to work for his chariots and horses
Send them to study under the priests
Give each of them land of their own

cards.text: Some sons will be his commanders of thousands and of fifties. Others will plow his ground, reap his harvest, and make his weapons and chariot gear.

cards.question: Samuel warns that the king will take their daughters too. What will he take them to be?

cards.text: BAKERS?! Somebody tell the king I'm booked. And he's not done: the best fields, vineyards and olive groves go to his servants.

cards.question: The king will take a ___ of their grain and grape harvest for his officials and servants.

cards.text: Then their menservants and maidservants, their best cattle and donkeys, and a tenth of their flocks. Take, take, take. This king has ONE word in his vocabulary.

cards.question: Samuel warns that in the end the people themselves will become the king's slaves.

cards.text: And when that day comes, Samuel says, they'll beg for relief from the king they've chosen.

cards.question: Samuel says that when the people beg for relief from their king, the LORD will answer them on that day.
Samuel has laid out the whole warning about the king. How do the people respond?

answers.text: They refuse to listen to Samuel
They ask Samuel for more time
They ask Samuel to be their king

cards.text: 'No!' they said. 'We must have a king over us.' That's the same energy I give my snooze button. The warning's right there on the screen, and I hit it ANYWAY.

cards.question: The people want a king to judge them, like all the other nations. What else do they say their king will do?

answers.text: Go out before them and fight their battles
Build them a great temple in the city
Bring the ark back to their camp

cards.text: Samuel listens to all the words of the people. Then he takes them back to the LORD. Every. Single. Word.

cards.question: The LORD tells Samuel to listen to their voice and appoint a ___ for them.

cards.text: Then Samuel tells the men of Israel, 'Everyone must go back to his city.' So Israel's getting a king. But WHO? Hang tight, friend. This story's just getting started.

findings.problem: The joke "I bet his knees crack louder than my oven door" is a joke about Samuel's age (old, creaky knees). That is a joke about age about a person in a Bible story, not about Papa Dorin himself.

rule.text: Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about age, gender, race, nationality, accents, appearance, intelligence or church denomination.

findings.problem: The setup line "so it's time to hand the job down" hints at an heir. That points toward "His sons" on card 2 and makes "His servants" and "His brothers" less likely.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has very little of Papa Dorin's humor. Only card 1 (the age joke) and card 6 (the referee) carry a real laugh. Cards 3, 11, 13 and 15 read as plain narration. Card 9's "Ooh" reads like a nice dad being pleasant. Moments that could hold a laugh without muddying a fact are left flat, including the elders' blunt "you are old," Samuel's displeasure, and the LORD looking all the way back to Egypt.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Solemnly warn them what the king will be like," stands out from the others. "Solemnly" is lifted from the BSB wording and sounds more like the Bible than "Make them fast and pray for forty days" or "Choose the king from his own family."

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
